prompt.context: LiquidCo is a private label liquids manufacturer. The company produces liquid-based products and sells them at drugstores like CVS and Duane Reade, and the products are then branded with these stores' names. For example, LiquidCo will produce mouthwash and hand sanitizer which is then branded with the CVS brand. Top line growth has been less than stellar. Revenue and volume growth is flat.
prompt.question: The CEO of LiquidCo has come to you to help them determine how they can grow. How would you approach this?

clarifying_info.q: What geographies does LiquidCo operate in?
clarifying_info.a: US only. LiquidCo cannot expand geographically since liquids are extremely expensive to ship, so the company would not be competitive internationally.

clarifying_info.q: Who are LiquidCo's current retail customers?
clarifying_info.a: LiquidCo currently sells to CVS, Duane Reade, Walmart, and various other retailers. They are not looking to expand to new drug stores or mass retailers as that is a small opportunity.

clarifying_info.q: What products does LiquidCo currently sell?
clarifying_info.a: Currently sells mouthwash, hand sanitizer, shampoo/conditioner, body lotion, and soaps.
No. Retailers have power in this area; prices cannot be increased. Current product mix should stay as is, but new products can be explored.
LiquidCo has excess capacity to produce more of certain liquids.

clarifying_info.q: What is the ownership situation and timeline?
clarifying_info.a: LiquidCo was recently bought by a PE firm that wants to see revenue growth as quickly as possible.

framework: Financial Assessment: Revenue = Price x Volume. Price increases blocked by retailer power; focus on Volume levers.
Volume — New retail channels: explore non-drugstore or non-mass retail channels (e.g., hotels, gyms, hospitals).
Volume — New products: launch adjacent liquid products (e.g., cough syrup, eye care / contact lens solution).
Volume — Geographic expansion: ruled out due to high shipping costs for liquids.
Volume — Own branded products: explore creating proprietary branded lines vs. private label only.
Channels: What outlets do we currently sell through? Would recommendations change the channel mix? Assess shelf space and pockets of opportunity.
Competition: Competitive landscape, market share, fragmented vs. concentrated, competitive response to any new launch.
Company capabilities: Financial capacity, production capacity (excess available), distribution network, people/training needs, risk of cannibalization.

questions.prompt: LiquidCo wants to explore a new product launch. What things would you want to consider?
questions.guidance: Candidate should go beyond a generic checklist and tie each factor specifically to LiquidCo's situation. Key areas: market size and growth rate; competitive landscape (number of competitors, market share, concentration); pricing dynamics; profitability (revenue and cost projections); size of investment required; raw materials sourcing; manufacturing requirements (new machinery needed? excess capacity available?); workforce/training implications; risk of cannibalization of existing product lines; competitive response.

questions.prompt: LiquidCo has identified two potential products to launch: 1) cough syrup and 2) eye care (contact lens solution). Which product would you recommend? (Interviewer gives data one piece at a time as candidate asks.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare addressable private-label market size, growth rates, capital requirements, competitive intensity, and operational fit. Cough syrup is preferred: larger addressable private-label market (~$12M vs ~$7.5M), higher private-label growth rate (6% vs 5-6%), uses existing facilities with no new capex, though faces a dominant competitor with 60% share. Eye care has a fragmented competitive landscape but requires a new sterile manufacturing facility (capital intensive) and carries recall risk, yielding a smaller private-label pool. Strong candidates will note the need to leverage current retailer relationships to gain shelf space for cough syrup given the dominant incumbent.

math.setup: Compare addressable private-label market revenue for each product. Cough Syrup: Total market $100M, 30% private label, LiquidCo can target 40% of that private-label share (remaining after incumbent's 60%). Eye Care: Total market $75M, 10% private label.
math.answer: Cough syrup addressable private-label opportunity is ~$12M vs. ~$7.5M for eye care. Recommend cough syrup.

questions.prompt: LiquidCo also wants to explore ideas for how the company can sell its main products (mouthwash, hand sanitizer, shampoo/conditioner, body lotion, soaps) to non-retailers. What ideas can you think of?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm non-drugstore / non-mass-retail channels where liquid personal care products are consumed or distributed. Interviewer should pressure-test 1-3 ideas even if feasible — best candidates defend their reasoning with logic rather than backing down. Categories: hospitality (hotels, airlines, airports), health and wellness (hospitals, gyms, yoga studios, cycling studios), education (schools), leisure/entertainment (malls, cinemas, bars/nightclubs).

brainstorming.prompt: What ideas can you think of for non-retailer channels where LiquidCo can sell its main products (mouthwash, hand sanitizer, shampoo/conditioner, body lotion, soaps)?

recommendation: Launch a private label cough syrup line — larger addressable private-label market (~$12M), higher private-label growth rate (6% annually), and leverages existing manufacturing facilities with no new capital investment required.
Expand current private label products to non-retailer channels such as hotels and gyms to increase sales of main products without jeopardizing existing retailer relationships.
risks: May not be able to gain significant market share against the dominant cough syrup private-label competitor who holds 60% share — LiquidCo must leverage current retailer relationships to secure shelf space or find a way to establish a cost advantage.
Non-retailer channel expansion requires sales team investment and channel development effort; success is uncertain.
next_steps: Meet with operations and manufacturing to determine the best way to implement production of cough syrup within existing facilities.
Meet with sales team to determine best approach for marketing cough syrup to current retail partners and securing shelf space.
Have sales team engage directly with retailers to negotiate cough syrup placement.
Investigate the market size opportunity for selling existing liquid products to non-retailers and identify which non-retailer segments to prioritize.
